title: Paint the middle nail on a silicone practice hand
instruction: Paint the middle fingernail on the silicone practice hand red. Keep the silicone around that nail clean.
context: Applying nail polish is a familiar home manicure. Painting the middle nail on a fixed practice hand isolates the skill of laying down a continuous coat without staining the skin.
setup: A fixed five-finger silicone practice hand rests on a dark gray 163 × 113 × 6 mm pad. Its wrist extends in +x, and its fingers point towards −x. The curved 17 × 12 mm middle nail is centred at (235, 0) mm on the centreline between the arm bases. A 23 g red applicator with a 27 × 24 × 38 mm handle and 5.6 mm effective tip starts upright at (163, 175) mm.
scoring: A held upright applicator must make measured tip contact with the nail or adjacent silicone. Full score requires at least 85% coverage and spill at most 2% of nail area for 0.3 s. Otherwise use coverage × max(0, 1 − 4 × spill), capped at 0.99.
reset_notes: Reset restores the fixed starting pose, returns the applicator upright and clears deposited polish.
fidelity: Native colliding applicator and nail surface. Deposited area uses a 0.75 mm grid and a swept foam footprint gated by tip contact. Foam flex, drying and pressure-dependent flow are simplified.
scores: Contact-gated revision awaits updated scripted and Dream-1 trials.
